title: GoodCook Everyday 100% Cotton Cheesecloth, 2 square yards, Bleached
description:
About this item
Make cheese, strain stocks and custard, bundle herbs or dust powdered sugar and cocoa.
Use 100% cotton cheesecloth in layers for added strength. Bleached cheesecloth has been processed to remove impurities of natural cotton fibers.
Butter-blanket a turkey for super juicy results.
2 Square yds. of food grade cheesecloth. Lint free and oven safe to 400°F.
Also great for cleaning, polishing and other household uses.

reviews_5s:
I am not using these for the intended purpose, so I can't say how well they work as cooking cheesecloth. The weave is fairly tight and the sheets wash well (I've washed them once a week for about 2 months and they are still as good as new, maybe just a bit more wrinkled and softer). With all this said, I am using them as towels to hang around my neck when I do my daily treadmill/exercise workout because I can't stand the thickness of other cotton towels and I just don't like the microfiber ones, and I wanted something that draped around my neck and fell somewhere around mid sternum (I'm 5'2"). I cut the sheets long-wise into two strips and then doubled each one over again. I hang them around my neck while I exercise. I look pretty different compared to the folks who like to dress up in name brand swag just to go exercise, but I definitely don't look like I've got a sheet of cheesecloth around my neck--just a thin white (yes, white, not natural or beige) towel.It's perfect for what I bought it for. I bought it to junk journal, to add texture. It's very thin, you can see through it. It's basically like guaze. But it's perfect for what I'm using it for. I'll definitely order more.It seems to be difficult to find this cloth. I use it for straining and soaking it in bourbon and wrap beef for dry aging because the cloth is able to breath. Other ones I have came across and purchased were canvas style material. I a dedicated fridge just for dry aging. The last one I aged, the cheese cloth was soaked in bulleit bourbon and turned put amazing.Does what cheesecloth does.
I use it to filter my fryer oil.It's very hard to clean the cheesecloth. I look at it as a disposable item. It works great to clean outvout little particles. I have used it while making maple syrup and for making wine. Very thin so it's a little hard to use by yourself.Great product for the price! This cheesecloth is just the right durability for all my cooking and other uses this cheesecloth is used for. Highly recommend.I thought I’d need two but only one was large enough for me. I got exactly what I paid for (:I bought it to make little ghost and they turned out super cute!I saw a decoration tip in a magazine about taking cheesecloth, tearing/making small holes in it, and then using that as a tablecloth (or on the wall or whatever) to look like cobwebs. This cheesecloth is PERFECT for that. It is very delicate, has a very loose weave, and is a good size (roughly 1 yard by 2 yards, roughly). Just run your fingertips over it to create the holes/tears, it's very easy. My kids love it, and I don't have to worry about pieces of polyester fake spider webs ending up on the floor where the baby can get a hold of it. This was a great buy!Well made. Sturdy. Works great for catching wax caps during honey extraction. It also withstands the boiling temp required to melt and process the wax.

I try to find GoodCook brand every year.

It's a help in making stocks or ciders too. The spices stay right where they are needed.
reviews_1s:
First, regarding Amazon Logistics: Quick delivery, arrived quite unexpectedly a day sooner than predicted, delivery driver's summary states the parcel was handed directly to the recipient when it was actually found on the floor outside my apartment door.

Second, this product is junk. The full 2 sq feet is comprised of a single narrow and very long strip of airy gauze, with a mesh too wide open to be useful for straining or containing anything without doubling or even tripling layers, and too small in width to allow for secure wrapping and tying. This is what people who don't know what cheesecloth is think cheesecloth is.Why didn't I read the reviews??!! This is absolutely not cheesecloth used for straining cheese. This is gauze and unless you use several layers, you can't use it to properly strain anything. Very disappointed, but as someone else wrote in their review: "You get what you pay for."It is pure garbage and a waste of time and money. I have never bought products and regrets spending my money; it is better to buy a T-Shirt, cut it and use it.

Using this cheesecloth is like using a regular filter.Very poor quality. I could have used a gauze bandage from my first aid kit. Mesh was uneven in spots, making it inconsistent for filtration. Left pieces of gauze behind. Never buying this again.The cloth wasn't tough enough to help strain the oats. After applying light pressure, It busted in multiple places AND when I was done it refused to allow me to clean it. had to toss it out.Poor quality. Not reusable. Waste of moneyThis is NOT cheese cloth. It's gauze. And not even good gauze. Don't buy this product.Did not serve my purpose because I wanted to make paneer.Would not call this cheese cloth, complete waste of money.Flimsy, overpriced. Comments noted that there were four for the price. That would have been great. One item (fell apart on first use and didn't strain) at $5.90 was terribly overpriced.
